verdicts.summary: The note says a hung managed server can still be stopped from the UI. That is wrong when the server's JS thread is stuck. The stop script only sends SIGTERM and fails if the PID is still alive after 2s. The server handles SIGTERM in JS (runMain plus process.on SIGTERM), so a blocked event loop never acts on it. Reconnect and disconnect then both fail, and the user has no way to recover. Before this change, reconnect sent the same kill, then cleared the PID and port and launched a fresh server.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The managed t3 server's event loop is blocked for good (a deadlock or a synchronous loop; it is alive and not a zombie). 2) The forward goes stale and ensureEnvironment reruns the launch script. 3) tunnel.ts:711 server_running is true and RUNNER_CHANGED=0, so tunnel.ts:720 waits 60s, then tunnel.ts:721-722 prints 'left running' and exits 1. 4) The user clicks disconnect. tunnel.ts:780-781 sends SIGTERM and the process does not exit, because its handler at apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:413 and NodeRuntime.runMain (binCli.ts:98) never get to run. tunnel.ts:787-789 exits 1 with 'did not stop within 2 seconds', and the ownership files are kept. 5) Every later reconnect repeats step 3. The same dead end happens if the PID was recycled: the runtime file and the pid file name the same reused PID (tunnel.ts:671), and nothing listens on the port.
verdicts.consequence: The remote environment stays unusable. Each reconnect fails after about 60s, disconnect fails, and the user has to SSH in and kill the process by hand.

verdicts.summary: The entry is removed from the map before its scope is closed, and the two steps are not wrapped together as uninterruptible. Disconnect does wrap them (tunnel.ts:1782-1785). If the caller interrupts between the two steps, the entry's scope never closes. The entry scope is a standalone Scope.make, and the manager finalizer only closes entries still in the map, so the ssh -N forward process and its local port leak.
verdicts.scenario: 1) An entry exists and the 2s probe at tunnel.ts:1656 fails. 2) tunnel.ts:1676 deletes the key. 3) The ensureEnvironment fiber is interrupted, for example by a request cancel or a timeout, before or inside the closeTunnelEntry call at tunnel.ts:1677 (whether interruption can land at this exact yield is inferred from Effect semantics, not observed). 4) entryScope (tunnel.ts:1558, Scope.make, not a child of the manager scope) is never closed. The manager finalizer at tunnel.ts:1401-1404 iterates tunnels.values() and misses it. Before this change, the entry stayed in the map, so a later call or shutdown closed it.
verdicts.consequence: An orphaned local ssh forward process keeps the local port bound until the app exits. The remote server's stop is also skipped at shutdown.

verdicts.summary: An adopted server that dies during the handover is no longer counted as running, and the fallback probe sends it on to a relaunch. Recorded managed PIDs are still killed only through REMOTE_PID.
verdicts.scenario: Managed marker present and REMOTE_PID alive. The runtime file names a service that answers the first probe and then exits, leaving a zombie. Line 679 kills our REMOTE_PID, and the state becomes external with ADOPTED_PID set to the service PID. At line 704, server_running sees ps stat Z and returns 1. Line 706's 2s wait_ready on the dead port fails, so REMOTE_PORT is cleared and line 729 launches a new server. I also tried a managed marker without a PID file while our own server is alive and named in the runtime file. It is adopted as external and no longer stopped on disconnect, but that is the intended 'no managed record' behaviour and the tests cover it.
